title: performance-canary: add automated latency/throughput regression detector and rollout guards
author: Priya Nair
commits: a1f4c2c: implement initial regression detector and alerting hooks
b3d9e7a: add rollout guard rules and canary policy integration
c7f1b22: add unit + integration tests for detector and hysteresis logic
d4e8a99: update perf-check CI job to run nightly with histograms and baselines
e5a2d08: docs: add canary behaviour and operator guidance
description:
Summary: Adds an automated detector that continuously monitors canary task latency and throughput against rolling baselines and triggers rollout guards when regressions are detected. Motivation: we saw multiple incidents where subtle latency regressions bypassed manual checks during rollouts; this PR codifies detection and automatic guardrails to prevent bad model/service variants from reaching production at scale.

What this implements: 1) a detector that computes distribution-aware comparisons (p95/p99 and throughput per-second) against an exponentially weighted rolling baseline and flags statistically significant regressions with configurable sensitivity; 2) hysteresis and KV-cache-aware thresholds to avoid noisy false positives during cold-cache windows; 3) rollout guard integration that can automatically pause or rollback canary traffic when regression thresholds are breached, with operator-facing reasons and metrics links; 4) CI integration: a perf-check job that runs canary-style workloads nightly and on PRs affecting the runtime; 5) unit/integration tests and operator docs.

Design notes: - Detector uses bootstrap-based confidence intervals for p95/p99 to be robust to non-normal latency distributions. - Separate counters for cold-cache vs warm-cache windows; detection is gated to require sustained regression across N minutes or M request count to reduce flaps. - Rollout guards have two modes: "pause" (stop traffic increase) and "rollback" (automated rollback for severe regressions). Both record reasons and link to recent histograms in the console. - Config is hierarchical: global defaults in src/perf/canary/config.yaml and per-deployment overrides via helm chart.

Testing: Includes deterministic unit tests for statistical logic and an integration test that runs a simulated workload against a toy model to exercise hysteresis. Nightly perf job was updated to produce baselines and alert on anomalies.

Backwards compatibility: Config defaults are conservative; operators must opt-in to automatic rollback.

Related: ENG-4821 (perf canary roadmap), ENG-4850 (rollout guard policy), SUP-992 (support ticket with incident notes that motivated this work).

review_comments: Samir Gupta (2026-01-19): Foundations look good. Two requests: 1) make hysteresis window configurable per-deployment, 2) add a developer-facing flag to disable auto-rollback for canaries in non-critical tiers.
Priya Nair (2026-01-19): Responded: added per-deployment hysteresis config and a 'rollback_mode' param (none/pause/rollback). Updated tests to cover the developer flag.
Lena Ortiz (2026-01-20): Tests are thorough. Question: how do we avoid false positives during model cold-starts? Suggest tracking cache-warmth and requiring X% warm requests before evaluating p99.
Priya Nair (2026-01-20): Implemented cache-warmth gating (requires 75% warm requests by default) and exposed it via config. Added extra integration test to simulate cold-start behavior.
Kai Nakamura (2026-01-22): Left an approval after verifying perf-check pipeline and manual simulation. Noted one nit in docs about how to interpret histogram links.
Samir Gupta (2026-01-24): Approved. Verified CI pass and nightlies are green after threshold tuning. Recommend rolling out to staging for 2 weeks before enabling auto-rollback in prod.
release_notes: Added automated canary regression detector, configurable hysteresis and KV-cache gating, and rollout guards (pause/rollback). Nightly perf-check CI updated to produce baselines and flag regressions. Operators must review and opt-in for auto-rollback.
